subject: Bridging proposal for Q2 overage and invoice smoothing
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena@finedge.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected Q2 invoice & reconciliation request

Hi Stephanie and Ben,

We just received the Aug invoice that includes a large Q2 true-up (line item: one-time overage of $48,600). This is the first we've seen of a post-period reconciliation at this scale — it wasn't flagged in the usage reports we reviewed during renewal. Can you help reconcile what drove this and whether any smoothing/crediting is possible?

Attached is our internal usage extract for Q2 (FinEdge_Q2_usage.csv). Key asks:
- Short summary of the spike: root cause and dates
- Whether any credits or one-time adjustments are available
- If we can spread an unavoidable charge over a few months instead of a single invoice

We'd like to avoid a surprise P&L hit this quarter; happy to hop on a quick call if useful.

Thanks,
Elena Morris
CFO, FinEdge
elena@finedge.com

Attachment: FinEdge_Q2_usage.csv (CSV)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@finedge.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected Q2 invoice & reconciliation request

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and for the usage extract. I've reviewed the file and flagged the high-volume bursts on May 17–19 that pushed total token consumption outside the committed bucket. Preliminary findings:
- Root cause: a batch inference job on a prod queue re-ran due to a downstream retry loop; the automatic KV caching didn't cover short-lived batch jobs, which increased per-token counts for those three days.
- Impact: roughly 1.1M extra prompt+completion tokens (~$48.6k).

Proposal to resolve quickly:
1) One-time bridging credit: Redwood applies a $20k credit to offset part of the spike (we can issue this as a credit memo).
2) Invoice smoothing: we will amortize the remaining $28.6k over 3 months by reissuing a smaller supplemental invoice for Sept/Oct/Nov (three equal installments).
3) Operational follow-up: our Solutions team will run a short config change to prevent the retry-loop pattern and add a 72-hour usage alert for burst anomalies.

I've attached a short proposal PDF with the math and a suggested amortization schedule. If that looks OK to you, Ben will coordinate the formal amendment and Laura will finalize the credit memo.

Next steps:
- Elena: confirm acceptance of the $20k credit + 3-month amortization
- Laura: prepare credit memo and a revised invoice schedule
- Ben/Stephanie: send an amendment that updates the true-up handling and documents the operational remediation

Happy to jump on a call if you want to run through the numbers.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0132

Attachment: RI_Proposed_Bridge_Credit.pdf (PDF)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Bridging proposal for Q2 overage and invoice smoothing

Internal notes / suggested language for amendment:

Stephanie — I like the $20k credit + amortization. A couple of operational points for Laura/finance:
- We should issue the credit as a credit memo referencing invoice INV-20260829-RECON and apply it against the August invoice. Then generate three small invoices labelled SUPP-SEP/OT/NOv tying back to DEAL-4832.
- For auditors: include a short explanation ("post-period reconciliation due to transient batch retry; credit provided as goodwill; remaining amount amortized per customer request").
- Ask Legal if the amendment should be a short sideletter vs. an SOW amendment. My preference: sideletter for speed, SOW for any change to consumption terms.

I'll start the amendment draft and loop Legal if needed. Laura — can you confirm the journal entries and whether we need a PO amendment from FinEdge? If they need a PO update, we'll ask them to sign the amortization schedule.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

> Attachment: draft_amort_schedule.xlsx (referenced)

From: Elena Morris <elena@finedge.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv@finedge.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bridging proposal for Q2 overage and invoice smoothing

Thanks, Stephanie and Ben. The $20k credit + amortization is acceptable to our finance team provided we get a revised invoice that spreads the remainder across Sept–Nov and a short note that this is a one-time accommodation. A few quick items:
- Can you confirm no SLA or service-level credits are charged against this event? We don't need penalty credits — just clarity for our controller.
- Please provide a one-page summary we can attach to our board pack explaining the cause and the remediation steps.

If you send the revised invoices and credit memo, we'll process the first installment on receipt.

Elena

Notes:
- This is documented as a one-time accommodation and does not alter committed bucket sizes or future true-up mechanics.
- No SLA deductions are being applied to this reconciliation.
- Laura, please route CM-20260902 to accounting and confirm when the credit has been posted.

Thanks everyone — let me know if you want a short sync.

Best,
